title: Residue logarithmic cotangent quotient and finite characteristic cokernel
statement: Let $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ be log smooth between locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ over $\bar y$ and a chart $Q\to N$ with $Q$ sharp fs. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, $C=\overline M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$, and $D=C/\operatorname{im}(Q^{\rm gp})$; geometric stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The relative logarithmic differential module $\omega_f$ is generated over $\mathcal O_X$ by $du$ for regular functions and $d\log m$ for log sections, with additivity, the Leibniz rule, $d\log(mm^{\prime})=d\log m+d\log m^{\prime}$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and vanishing of $du$ and $d\log m$ for sections pulled back from the base. There is a surjection $$\pi:k\otimes_A\omega_{f,\bar x}\longrightarrow k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}D$$ taking $1\otimes d\log t$ to $1\otimes[t]$ and $1\otimes du$ to zero. There exist finitely many $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ whose classes $1\otimes[t_i]$ form a $k$-basis of $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}D$. For any such choice, $C/(\sum_i\mathbf Z[t_i]+\operatorname{im}Q^{\rm gp})$ is finite, killed by some positive integer $n$ invertible in $A$. For every positive integer $a$ invertible in $A$, the group $A^\times$ is $a$-divisible, meaning each of its elements is an $a$th power of a unit. The empty basis is allowed.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, map (1), choice of t_i and finite cokernel C; divisibility of strict local units in the paragraph preceding diagram (3).

proof.text: First identify the geometric structure-sheaf stalk $A$ with the pointed-affine-neighbourhood ring colimit of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Indeed, [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] defines the stalk using all pointed etale neighbourhoods, and [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal] allows restriction to the affine ones; choosing their small representative subcategory is exactly the colimit in the former definition. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure] applies to $X,\bar x$: $A$ is local and strictly henselian. In particular [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] says that $A$ is henselian and $k$ is separably closed. No assertion that $k$ is the full field of the chosen geometric point is needed.

proof.text: Use an fs chart $P\to M$ near $\bar x$, as supplied by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The chart's stalk pushout says that every log element is a chart element times a unit. Consequently the images of a finite monoid generating set of $P$ generate $\overline M_{\bar x}$, and their classes generate $C$ as an abelian group. Their images therefore generate $D$. This uses only the fs chart definition, not the existence of a chart specially adapted to $f$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, pp.136--137, characteristic groups in map (1); finite generation from the fine chart definition.

proof.text: Define the proposed $A$-linear map from the presented module $\omega_{f,\bar x}$ to $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}D$ (with the residue $A$-action) by $du\mapsto0$ and $d\log m\mapsto1\otimes[m]$. Check every relation in the statement. Additivity and Leibniz map to zero, and multiplicativity of $d\log$ maps to addition in the group $D$. For $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, if $\alpha(m)$ is a nonunit its residue coefficient is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion]; if it is a unit, the log-structure condition of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives $[m]=0$ in $C$. Thus this relation also maps to zero. The base relations vanish: a chart $Q\to N$ identifies every base log element at $\bar y$ with a chart element times a base unit; its image in $C$ lies in $\operatorname{im}Q^{\rm gp}$, since ring maps take units to units. Hence the map factors through $\pi:k\otimes_A\omega_{f,\bar x}\to k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}D$. The formula extends additively to $d\log t$ for $t\in M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$. Every element of $D$ lifts to this group, so pure tensors, and therefore the whole target, are in the image. This proves the asserted surjection.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, map (1), pp.136--137; the check of the displayed logarithmic differential relations is expanded here.

proof.text: The finite generating family of $D$ from Step 2 gives a finite spanning family $1\otimes d_j$ of $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}D$. Traverse it in order, retaining a vector exactly when it is not in the span of the retained vectors. The retained list is independent by construction and spans the original list, hence is a basis. Lift its elements $d_j$ through $M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}\twoheadrightarrow D$ to get $t_1,\ldots,t_r$. If the vector space is zero, the retained list is empty.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, p.137, choice of the t_i immediately after (2); finite spanning-set elimination written out.

proof.text: Now fix any choice with the stated basis property, not just the one of Step 4, and put $E=C/(\sum_i\mathbf Z[t_i]+\operatorname{im}Q^{\rm gp})$. This is a finitely generated abelian group, as it is a quotient of the finitely generated group $C$. The map $D\twoheadrightarrow E$ induces a surjection on tensors: each pure tensor $b\otimes e$ lifts by choosing a lift of $e$, and pure tensors generate. But the spanning vectors $1\otimes[t_i]$ all map to zero, so this tensor map is zero. Thus $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}E=0$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, p.137, surjectivity of k(x) tensor the map u and the assertion about its cokernel; the tensor argument expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure] to $E$. It is a finite direct sum of a free group $\mathbf Z^s$ and cyclic groups of prime-power orders $q_j^{e_j}$. If $s>0$, projection onto a free coordinate defines a nonzero balanced pairing $k\times E\to k$, $(b,e)\mapsto b\,\overline{\operatorname{pr}(e)}$; it induces a nonzero map $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}E\to k$, contrary to Step 5. Hence $s=0$ and $E$ is finite. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, any summand of order $p^{e_j}$ with $e_j>0$ similarly gives a nonzero pairing by projection and reduction $\mathbf Z/p^{e_j}\to\mathbf F_p\subset k$. Thus there is no such summand. Take $n=\prod_jq_j^{e_j}$, with the empty product equal to $1$. It kills $E$ and has nonzero residue in $k$: in characteristic zero every positive integer does, and in characteristic $p$ none of its factors is $p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], $n$ is invertible in $A$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, p.137, cokernel killed by m invertible in k(x); abelian structure theorem explicitly supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Let $a>0$ be invertible in $A$ and let $u\in A^\times$. By Step 1, $k$ is separably closed. The polynomial $T^a-\bar u$ has nonzero constant term, and its derivative is $\bar aT^{a-1}$, with $\bar a\ne0$. These two polynomials have no common root (a root of the first is nonzero); equivalently their greatest common divisor is $1$, so the polynomial is separable. By [def-pc-separably-closed] it has a root $v_0\in k$, necessarily nonzero, and its derivative at $v_0$ is nonzero. The simple-root implication of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting], using henselianity from Step 1, lifts $v_0$ to $v\in A$ with $v^a=u$. Since $v$ has nonzero residue, [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion] makes $v$ a unit. This proves $a$-divisibility for every permitted $a$, including $a=1$, independently of the particular $n$ in Step 6.
